_comment: temper-rust-router-core's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json and
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json. Same contract, same reasoning -- see
wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed
rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because
run_wasm_tests.mjs exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no
registered test. Point the runner at this one with
`--expected-failures tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json` when the
module carries temper-rust-router-core alone (`make wasm-router-core-test` does).
Native baseline, for contrast: `cargo test --manifest-path
packages/temper-rust-router-core/Cargo.toml` passes 154/155 (1 ignored) on
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, all 23 of these included. Every entry below is therefore a
genuine native-vs-wasm32 divergence, not a broken test.
Measured 2026-08-10 against 111 registered tests: 88 pass, 23 expected-fail, 0 other.
All 23 are ONE class and ONE root cause: the rewrite engine reads the clock. That is
the `no-clock` class temper-geometry already catalogues, and as there the panic is in
PRODUCTION code rather than in a test -- so the honest reading is 'combinator::rewrite
does not run on wasm32 yet', not '23 flaky tests'. Making it run means gating the
RewriteTrace timing behind a target that has a clock; that is a change to the rewrite
engine and is deliberately NOT bundled into a registration-only PR.
THE FOLLOW-UP IS ALREADY PRECEDENTED. PR #941 did exactly this for temper-geometry:
build_capacitated_graph took its deadline Instant lazily (only when a deadline was
actually requested) and 7 of that crate's 8 `no-clock` entries turned into passes,
reconciled by #942. rewrite() is the same shape but a wider change: ~10 Instant::now()
sites whose Durations are consumed only by trace.log(), which is gated on the
TEMPER_REWRITE_TRACE env var -- but the format! arguments are evaluated eagerly, so
every reading happens even when tracing is off. Making them lazy is a refactor of the
SAT pipeline's rewrite engine and belongs in its own PR with its own A/B.
The gate is bidirectional: if one of these starts passing (someone gives
RewriteTrace a wasm32 path), run_wasm_tests.mjs reports it as an UNEXPECTED PASS and
exits non-zero, so a stale exclusion cannot sit here unnoticed.

combinator::integration::tests::roundtri.reason: Drives the full model -> rewrite -> CNF pipeline, so it reaches the unconditional Instant::now() inside rewrite()'s RewriteTrace (see the combinator::rewrite entries below for the mechanism). Nothing about the test is wasm32-specific; it never gets past the first rewrite() call.

combinator::integration::tests::audit_co.reason: Same root cause: the audit round-trip calls rewrite(), which reads the clock before doing any work.

combinator::integration::tests::no_regre.reason: Same root cause: the at-most-k regression fixture is fed through rewrite().
Same root cause: the differential-pair regression fixture is fed through rewrite().

combinator::rewrite::tests::rw7_layer_co.reason: Calls combinator::rewrite::rewrite(), whose RewriteTrace::new() (combinator/rewrite.rs:73) evaluates `start: Instant::now()` unconditionally -- the struct is constructed on every call, before the `enabled` flag is consulted, so the TEMPER_REWRITE_TRACE env var does not gate it. rewrite() then takes six further Instant::now() readings for its per-rule timing breakdown. wasm32-unknown-unknown's std has no clock: Instant::now() panics with 'time not implemented on this platform' (library/std/src/sys/time/unsupported.rs:13). This is the root entry; the other rewrite entries are the same fact reached through different rules.

combinator::rewrite::tests::rw7_no_confl.reason: Same root cause as rw7_layer_conflict_detected: rewrite()'s RewriteTrace reads the clock before any rule runs.
